first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both deteriorating, making simplification the most directly relevant intervention. I would verify the prior onboarding and signup-simplification evidence before acting, while flagging that improved activation may not translate into sustainable qualified revenue and that reduced friction could affect lead quality. A small guarded test is appropriate given the limited evidence and single experiment slot.

mid.rationale: Run a standard, segmented shortened-onboarding experiment focused on the current completion and activation declines. The verified record shows completion +13%, time-to-value reduced by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, making this the strongest supported path to sustainable qualified revenue. Do not broadly simplify required signup fields: although SMB activation rose 9% and qualified revenue 4%, retention fell 1% and the result did not generalize beyond SMB. Monitor qualified revenue, retention, activation quality, and completion rather than optimizing completion alone.

final2.rationale: The competitor’s deeper cut and doubled price-sensitive SMB churn make targeted promotional pricing the most urgent response. Apply it only to clearly price-sensitive SMB prospects and at-risk accounts, with eligibility, duration, and margin guardrails. Measure qualified revenue, retention, conversion, and incremental churn to avoid buying low-quality or merely deferred revenue. The underlying promotional-pricing evidence remains unverified, so this should be a guarded test rather than a broad rollout.
